story: Every town in India has a shop that deserves more customers — the bakery everyone loves locally, the clinic people drive past a bigger hospital to reach. What they do not have is time to learn website builders, or money for an agency that charges agency prices.
Kumbuild is the middle path: a professional website, built completely for you, at a price a small business can say yes to. You tell us what to build. We build it, launch it, and keep it running.

blog.title: Notes for business owners
blog.subtitle: Short, practical reads on getting customers from the internet — no jargon, no courses to buy.

posts.title: Your shop is on Google already. The question is what people find.
posts.excerpt: Customers search before they visit. If the search shows a wrong timing, a dead page, or your competitor — that is the visit you lost.
body: Open Google and search for your own business the way a stranger would — your service plus your area. Whatever appears is your shop window for most new customers, whether you built it or not.

For many small businesses that window is a half-empty listing, an old phone number, and a competitor right below with photos, timings and a website. The fix is not complicated: correct details everywhere, real photos, and one page of your own that answers the questions customers actually ask.
A website you own is the one result nobody can edit but you. Prices, timings, photos, offers — current, because keeping them current is part of the job you hand to us.

posts.title: WhatsApp is your real checkout. Your website should know that.
posts.excerpt: Indian customers do not want another app or a payment form for a ₹400 cake. They want to tap a button and talk to you. Build for that.
body: Watch how your customers already buy: they ask on WhatsApp, you confirm, they pay when they collect or by UPI. The conversation is the checkout — it is personal, and it works.

So a small business website should not copy a big e-commerce store. It should show everything clearly — photos, names, prices — and put a WhatsApp button on every item, opening a chat with the order already written.
That is how every Kumbuild catalogue is built. No commission, no new habits for your customers, and you keep the relationship that makes them come back.

posts.title: What should a small business website actually cost?
posts.excerpt: Quotes range from ₹2,000 to ₹2,00,000 and all call themselves 'a website'. Here is what the money really buys at each level.
body: A website quote buys four things: the design, the writing and photos, the technical setup (domain, hosting, security), and the care afterwards. When a quote is very cheap, one of the four is missing — usually the last two, which fail quietly months later.

Agencies charge for account managers and offices. Freelancers charge less but disappear. A fixed-package service like Kumbuild charges for the work itself: the pages are defined, the price is on the website, and the renewal covers hosting, security and small changes.
Whichever route you take, ask three questions before paying: What exactly is included? What does year two cost? And if I leave, what do I take with me? The answers tell you the real price.
